purpose: Hand-authored content contexts (docs/foundation-graph-schema.md §2.2, step 8) for the skills the inline + content-map merge left short of >=3 contexts / >=2 families. Each is a real source in which the skill is genuinely exercised, chosen to add a source FAMILY the skill did not yet cover. Kept separate from the graph so the authored provenance is explicit (the builder tags these `authored`); when the graph is next re-authored these can fold into its inline sourceContexts. These are asserted, not pilot-validated — like all content claims they are subject to the educator audit.

fnd-orient-page-geography.why: the prayer text sits inside surrounding rubric and halakhic instructions — primary text vs. what wraps it, in a liturgical layout

fnd-orient-speaker.why: God calls 'Moses, Moses' and Moses answers 'Here am I' — identifying who speaks, in Torah narrative

fnd-orient-unit-boundary.why: a single se'if is a self-contained unit of ruling — marking where one unit of thought begins and ends, in a code

fnd-signal-name-formulas.why: 'Shimon HaTzaddik ... hu haya omer' is the same 'X said' attribution formula outside the Talmud — a second family for the skill

fnd-case-restate.why: Esau sells the birthright is a compact narrative case a learner can retell in their own words

fnd-agency-ask-question.ref: A studied berakhah or fixed prayer
fnd-agency-ask-question.why: asking a clear, answerable question about the wording or structure of a prayer

fnd-agency-use-tools.ref: A halakhic ruling traced to its Talmudic source
fnd-agency-use-tools.why: deliberately following a code's cross-reference back to the Gemara it rests on

fnd-agency-choose-next.ref: Choosing the next Torah portion to study
fnd-agency-choose-next.why: deciding and justifying the next study move within Tanakh, not only within Gemara
